newsitem.title: LATVIA: UNIBANKA TENDER TO BE SET ON THURSDAY.
newsitem.headline: UNIBANKA TENDER TO BE SET ON THURSDAY.

text.p: The Latvian Privatisation Agency (LPA) on Wednesday said it will set tender rules on Thursday to choose between 30 financial intermediaries to place part of the state's stake in Unibanka abroad.

The LPA earlier said it wants to sell all of its 33 percent stake in Unibanka, Latvia's second largest bank, of which 20 percent will be sold abroad, probably in the form of gross depsoitory receipts (GDRs).
"We will approve the rules for the tender, worked out by Coopers & Lybrand, on Thursday," Ilmars Razumovskis, the LPA's finance manager, told a news conference.
"We have already sent out invitations to more than 30 financial intermediaries," he added.
"Both Cooper & Lybrands and the LPA think the number of companies who have the qualifications to perform this task is limited," Janis Naglis, the LPA's general manager, said.
"The share capital adjustment after the bonus share issue must still be completed, which does not allow us to give exact figures for shares to be sold internationally," Razumovskis said.
The LPA is still waiting for approval from the Europan Bank for Reconstruction and Development, which also holds a big stake in Unibanka.
"The tender rules will therefore not yet specify the amount of shares to be placed nor will they be confined to GDRs," Razumovskis said.
"We will also place parts of the state's stakes in the Latvian Shipping Company, Ventspils Nafta oil terminal, Latvenergo energy company, Lattelekom and Latvian Gas abroad," Naglis added.
"The placer who succesfully completes a Unibanka programme might have some handicap when the next placement comes up, but the selections will be done separately for each company," Razumovskis said.
"We hope that this (international palcement) programme will alow shares of our companies to enter bourses in London, even New York perhaps or Frankfurt and Louxemburg," Naglis said.
